blocks.text: An interim briefing for the leadership team on the operating-model engagement. This is a read of where the work stands and what we are examining, not a set of conclusions; those come later, and only once the numbers behind them are settled with your people.

items: The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2011-001.start}} and is in its early weeks.
We are building the present-state read: how the business runs today across its main lines.
Nothing here is a recommendation. The design work comes after the present-state picture is settled.
Today is about sharing what we are examining and agreeing the questions worth pursuing next.
Jason Torres, Principal, leads the engagement and is your point of contact.
Deborah Allen, Consultant, carries the analysis and builds the exhibits behind it.
Sponsored on your side by Melissa Johnson, General Manager, who owns the data requests.
We start by listening, then set down the few judgments the operating model turns on.
Every recommendation will trace back to the evidence behind it, figure by figure.
Where the evidence supports only a range, we will say so instead of rounding it off to look finished.
The operating model as it runs today: the roles, the hand-offs, and the processes between them.
Where the online channels change what the work requires, and where they only add a step.
The cost-to-serve for each main line, so we can see what the present model actually costs.
Where the logic is consistent across lines, and where the same task is handled several ways.
Finish the present-state read across the remaining lines.
Pull the cost-to-serve for each line and reconcile it with your figures.
Keep data requests flowing through Melissa Johnson as a single consolidated list.
Agree the two or three questions the design should turn on.
